newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares seen moving sideways, lack of leads.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares seen moving sideways, lack of leads.

text.p: Jakarta shares are expected to moving sideways on Thursday due to the lack of fresh leads although focus should remain on newly-listed Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI), brokers said.
"The possibility for the index to rebound is relatively slim as several big-capitalised stocks are likely to continue undergoing some correction," a broker said.
But brokers said local investors were likely to pay attention to some secondaries which are the subject of rumours regarding mergers, take-overs and acquisitions.
Brokers said besides focus on the BNI, some investors could concentrate on the Initial Public Offering from Bank Umum Servitia.

Heavyweight Telkom was likely to continue under selling pressure on continued speculation that the goverment could do a secondary offering some time next year. "We could not confirm it during a conference call yesterday with the company but that talk remains in the market," a foreign analyst said.
On Wednesday, the Jakarta composite index fell 5.96 points, or 0.95 percent, to end at 620.27 points.
